title: Pre-existing buyers - do they get any protection under the new housing law
p1:
Booked your home before the new housing law came in? You may not be as unprotected as you think.

But there is a catch that many buyers overlook.
p2:
A common assumption is that a new housing law automatically applies only to agreements signed after it takes effect. That is not always the full picture.

Existing buyers may still receive protection depending on the law, the nature of the transaction, and whether their rights or obligations were already legally established.
p3:
The key question is not simply, “When did I buy?”

It is: “What right or obligation is being affected, and when did that right arise?”

This distinction can matter for possession, refunds, disclosures, interest, compensation, delayed projects, or remedies against a developer.

So if you are a pre-existing buyer, do not assume that the new law either fully protects you or completely excludes you. Check the transition provisions and how the law treats existing agreements.

That small detail can change the legal position significantly.
conclusion: If a buyer booked a property before a new housing law came into force, should the buyer automatically get its new protections? Or should the original agreement control? What do you think?
